versions.provenance: 8th edition colon and rectum TNM, rewritten from criteria published on Medscape/public references; interim content pending the licensed content and R1 clinical verification.
versions.introduction:
The 8th edition staging system applies to carcinomas of the colon and rectum. T describes depth of invasion through the bowel wall rather than tumour size, N is defined by the number of positive regional nodes together with tumour deposits, and M distinguishes single-site (M1a), multi-site (M1b), and peritoneal (M1c) metastasis. A minimum of 12 regional lymph nodes should be examined for adequate nodal staging.

8th edition refined the M category by splitting M1 into M1a, M1b and M1c, so that peritoneal metastasis (M1c) is now its own category, and it formalised the role of tumour deposits (N1c). Mismatch-repair / microsatellite-instability status and KRAS, NRAS and BRAF mutation status are recorded because they guide therapy, and for rectal cancer the circumferential resection margin and the tumour regression grade after neoadjuvant therapy carry additional prognostic weight.

t.label: Carcinoma in situ, intramucosal carcinoma (involves the lamina propria with no extension through the muscularis mucosae)
Tumour invades the submucosa (through the muscularis mucosae but not into the muscularis propria)
Tumour invades through the muscularis propria into the pericolorectal tissues
Tumour invades the visceral peritoneum or invades or adheres to an adjacent organ or structure

Tumour invades through the visceral peritoneum (including gross perforation of the bowel through tumour and continuous invasion of tumour through areas of inflammation to the surface of the visceral peritoneum)
Tumour directly invades or adheres to an adjacent organ or structure

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
1 to 3 regional lymph nodes are positive (tumour in a node >= 0.2 mm), or any number of tumour deposits are present and all identifiable lymph nodes are negative
2 or 3 regional lymph nodes are positive
No regional lymph nodes are positive, but there are tumour deposits in the subserosa, mesentery, or nonperitonealised pericolic or perirectal/mesorectal tissues
4 or more regional lymph nodes are positive
4 to 6 regional lymph nodes are positive
7 or more regional lymph nodes are positive

m.label: Metastasis to one site or organ is identified, without peritoneal metastasis
Metastasis to two or more sites or organs is identified, without peritoneal metastasis
Metastasis to the peritoneal surface is identified alone or with other site or organ metastasis

stageGroups.basis: Metastasis to two or more sites/organs

postNeoadjuvant.note: After neoadjuvant chemoradiation (common in rectal cancer), stage uses ypT/ypN/ypM applied to the same anatomic stage groups as the pathologic (p) table above.

versions.regionalNodes: Pericolic and perirectal nodes and the nodes along the named feeding vessels (ileocolic, right/middle/left colic, inferior mesenteric, sigmoid, superior rectal, and, for the rectum, the middle rectal and internal iliac nodes). At least 12 regional nodes should be examined; external and common iliac and para-aortic nodes are non-regional and count as distant metastasis.
versions.histologicGrade: G1 well differentiated, G2 moderately differentiated, G3 poorly differentiated, G4 undifferentiated; commonly collapsed into low grade (G1 to G2) versus high grade (G3 to G4). Mismatch-repair-deficient/MSI-high tumours are reported separately.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Adenocarcinoma accounts for the great majority. Recognised variants include mucinous (colloid) adenocarcinoma, signet-ring cell carcinoma, and medullary carcinoma, with less common adenosquamous, spindle-cell, and undifferentiated carcinomas. Neuroendocrine tumours are staged under a separate system.
prognosticFactors: T and N category (depth of invasion and number of positive nodes)
KRAS, NRAS and BRAF mutation status
Tumour regression grade after neoadjuvant therapy
